requirements.requirement: An individual binding affinity is measured under stated assay conditions; for the fictional one-to-one comparison lower KD means tighter binding.
Linked multiple contacts create avidity, with spacing and reconnection relevant to the observed interaction.
Multivalent apparent cell binding is not automatically single-site affinity; target density, spacing and assay preparation matter.
Native epitope accessibility is a separate question: folding or neighbouring material can block access despite target abundance or a recognized sequence.
Stability, aggregation and unwanted recognition/developability need separate tests from affinity.
A stronger measured interaction does not establish better delivery or a safer or more effective treatment; no universal optimum is depicted.
In the fictional A/B example 1 nM is tighter than 10 nM in the same assay, while different aggregation and native-cell evidence do not select a treatment.
An scFv links VH and VL variable domains by a peptide linker in one protein chain; one chain is not one variable domain.
The illustrated VHH is one variable domain without a VL partner; an isolated VHH differs from a complete heavy-chain antibody.
A recognition module, a whole antibody, a whole CAR and a living cell are different objects.
Linked domains must fold and recover actual binding in the tested construct; architecture alone does not show every linker or sequence works.
The size or appearance of a soluble recognition module does not determine transport of a cell carrying it.
Neither fragment architecture nor the schematic size establishes whole-product safety, useful function or comparative clinical performance.
The displayed fictional candidate B and its recoverable genetic instructions remain linked to the same carrier identity.
Unretained phage is a selection status, not proof of no binding or an established hit.
Recovery and sequencing identify the candidate; making a separate protein and measuring it add distinct steps.
Target, tag and negative controls test the identified protein outside its selection system; a tag-associated interaction is not established intended-target specificity.
Computational ranking is prediction followed by make-and-measure, not measured binding or clinical validation or a universal recovery rate.
The fictional 60 ranked, eight purified and two tag-binding candidates establish zero intended-target binders yet, without proving that none exists.

nonCanonicalChecks.requirement: Drawing colours, shapes, dimensions and ordinal panels are schematic identifiers, not atomic coordinates, biological scale or study quantities.
Both fragment alt/caption strings in provenance duplicate the pinned parent text verbatim; duplication is not extra scientific credit.

The immutable discovery brief retains its original outgoing-carrier wording; inverse substitution in current SVGs reproduces declared prior hashes without proving a historical author or execution time.
PASS, source/pixel reading claims, author identities, code/model-call claims, contrast metrics and keyboard observations remain at their actual documentary scope, without new approval.

The fragment parent has a substantive original/later mass-paragraph delta and a later body-versus-bibliography range discrepancy; masses and general clearance/penetration assertions are not inferred from the unscaled figure.
Current SVG text, object placement, panel sequence and labelled comparison are assessed in full in both themes; this is not a site/mobile/browser or accessibility acceptance.

sourceScope: Nine complete bodies, six freshly viewed associated SVG renders, three later parent bodies and exact original/later diffs. Parent-only numeric mass assertions are bounded context, not new ordinary-course coverage.
earlierNamedPartialReadForContext: SB18-062 concerns a general therapeutic nonprotein-target counterexample; the anti-digoxin binder citation is not assumed to resolve that therapeutic requirement.
